title: Cava Reported Revenue Increasing by 31%
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether Cava Group is an undervalued restaurant opportunity after a strong quarter. Cava's revenue rose 31% year over year, with 17 new restaurants taking the estate to 476 locations and same-store sales up 9%, driven by 5.3% traffic growth, so part of the growth is organic rather than just new openings. Trailing sales have climbed from roughly $500M in 2023 to about $1.37B, and he sees a long runway from under 500 Mediterranean locations toward 3,000-6,000 at maturity, in a market crowded with pizza, burger and burrito concepts. The problem is profitability: operating cash-flow margin has flatlined around 16% since 2025 as tariffs, oil and input costs lifted both opening and operating costs, and returns on invested capital, once approaching 15% and ahead of early-stage Chipotle, have stopped improving. He updated his discounted cash flow and revised estimates slightly higher, putting fair value at about $52 against a market price a little over $58, so even after a margin of safety the shares look slightly overvalued. The call is CAVA — HOLD, low conviction, his first tracked Cava call; he is watching for margin improvement to resume while revenue keeps expanding. One forward price-to-sales figure is garbled in the auto-captions.

calls.price_at_call: trading a little over $58 (stated); DCF fair value $52 (stated)
calls.thesis: HOLD, low conviction, first tracked CAVA call for Parkevtate (no prior CAVA call in calls.json, so no flip) — he says Cava is not a buying opportunity right now: even after the de-rating the stock looks slightly overvalued, with his revised DCF at ~$52 vs a market price a little over $58. Revenue rose 31% in the latest quarter (17 new stores to 476; same-store sales +9% on +5.3% traffic), but operating cash-flow margin has flatlined around 16% since 2025 on tariff, oil and input-cost inflation, so he is watching for margin improvement to resume alongside revenue growth.
